sources.title: New guidebook for Istria & Kvarner

sections.heading: Destination Snapshot
sections.body: Istria and Kvarner make a broad northern-Adriatic sport-climbing region, with compact crags, coastal rest days and enough variety to fill more than one trip.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Destination Snapshot.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
This is a regional sport-climbing page rather than one crag. The current Istria and Kvarner guidebook covers crags across Croatia, with additional nearby areas and islands included in the wider circuit.

The appeal is variety: canyon crags, coastal venues, inland limestone and a large enough route base that mixed teams can move around with the weather and energy levels.

sections.heading: History And Reputation
sections.body: The area has had active local development and repeated guidebook updates, with routes checked, rephotographed and reorganized for the current Istria and Kvarner coverage.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for History And Reputation.

sections.heading: Rock And Climbing Character
sections.body: Expect sport climbing on limestone, with the exact character changing from crag to crag. The region includes slabs, vertical technical walls, steeper sectors and cave-style climbing, so it is worth choosing venues by style rather than just by grade.

sections.heading: Who It Suits
sections.body: Istria works well for sport climbers who want a flexible holiday base and the option to change crags. It is especially useful for teams that want climbing, sea, food and rest-day options in the same trip.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Who It Suits.

sections.heading: Grades And Scale
sections.body: The current regional guidebook covers 36 crags and more than 2,000 routes. That scale makes Istria a destination for a full climbing holiday rather than a short stop at one famous sector.

sections.heading: Season
sections.body: Spring and autumn are the cleanest bets for conditions. Summer can be hot, so shade, wind and coastal timing become important if you climb then.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Season.

warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Gear.

sections.heading: Getting There
sections.body: A car is the practical choice. The crags are spread across the region, and the best venue on a given day may depend on sun, wind, grade and rest-day plans.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Getting There.

warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Where To Stay.

sections.heading: Rest Days
sections.body: The region is set up for rest days, with coastal towns, food, nature and island options close enough to combine with a climbing trip.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Rest Days.

sections.heading: Local Tips And Rules
sections.body: Use the guidebook by crag character. The best day is usually not the nearest crag; it is the one with the right aspect, style and difficulty mix for the team.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Local Tips And Rules.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Treat fixed gear and access as crag-specific. The region has many separate venues, so local notes matter more than broad assumptions.
warnings: No sufficiently specific sourced content for Safety.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Istria one climbing area? No. It is a regional sport-climbing circuit.

How many routes are covered? The current guidebook lists more than 2,000 routes across 36 crags.

Do you need a car? Yes, for a normal trip.
